auth: Authorization: Bearer <MCP token> (jolt_live_..., from POST /v1/mcp-tokens). App tokens are refused: opening /mcp/sse answers 401, tool calls fail.
errors: Tools whose output_schema is a union with {error} return that object for recoverable problems. Any other failure (missing/invalid token, unknown source, invalid grade) is raised and arrives as an MCP tool error (isError: true) with the message as text.

tools.name: jolt_get_tracks
tools.description:
List the study tracks visible to the caller: their own tracks plus the world-readable curated ('jolt') tracks. A track is a subject/course that concepts hang off of.
Arguments: none.
Returns: { tracks: [ { id, name, origin, kind, archived, syllabus, agenda } ] } where `origin` is 'user' or 'jolt' (curated, read-only), `kind` is 'notes' or 'dsa_patterns', and `archived` is true for a track the learner paused (do not file new concepts there unless the note clearly belongs to it). `syllabus` is a flat list of the agenda's topic labels (convenience). `agenda` is the full track agenda: { status ('none'|'draft'|'refined'|'locked'), source ('agent'|'user'|'emergent'), syllabus: [ { concept_key, label, parent, source } ], last_refined_at, refined_from_source_id, outline }. An agenda with status 'draft', source 'user' and an `outline` is a rough outline the learner typed when creating the track: tidy it into a proper syllabus with jolt_set_agenda (mark_refined=true) during this sync, keeping the learner's topics. Use a track `id` as `track_id` for the agenda, concept, coverage, question, and extraction tools. Read-only.

tools.name: jolt_get_recent_concepts
tools.description:
List a track's most recently created concepts, newest first — use it to see what already exists before logging a session, so you extend coverage instead of duplicating concepts.
Arguments:
  track_id (str, required) — the track to read, from jolt_get_tracks.
  limit (int, optional, default 20) — max concepts to return.
Returns: { concepts: [ { id, text, title, syllabus_ref } ] }. `syllabus_ref` is the agenda concept_key the concept is filed under, or null. Only the caller's own concepts are listed (on a curated track, the ones they logged). Raises if the track is neither the caller's nor curated. Read-only.

tools.name: jolt_get_coverage
tools.description:
Report how well the caller's studied concepts cover a track's syllabus — the signal for what to study or extract next.
Arguments:
  track_id (str, required) — the track to measure, from jolt_get_tracks.
Returns: { track_id, total_concepts, studied_concepts, decaying_concepts, off_plan_concepts, coverage_ratio (0..1), uncovered_syllabus: [concept_keys] }. `studied_concepts` are those the user has an FSRS memory state for; `decaying_concepts` are studied ones whose recall has weakened or fallen due; `uncovered_syllabus` lists syllabus keys with no studied concept yet. `off_plan_concepts` are concepts on a LOCKED track whose key is not in the syllabus (auto-add is skipped there): they are kept and reviewed but left out of every other count. Raises if the track is neither the caller's nor curated. Read-only.

tools.name: jolt_get_agenda
tools.description:
Get a track's agenda — its shaped syllabus and refinement lifecycle. Call this before refining (jolt_set_agenda) so you EXTEND the existing syllabus rather than replace it, and to check whether the agenda is locked (a locked agenda rejects every write).
Arguments:
  track_id (str, required) — the track to read, from jolt_get_tracks.
Returns: { status ('none'|'draft'|'refined'|'locked'), source ('agent'|'user'|'emergent'), syllabus: [ { concept_key, label, parent, source } ], last_refined_at, refined_from_source_id, outline }, or { error } if the track is not the caller's (or curated). `concept_key` is the stable key a concept's syllabus_ref points at; `parent` (another item's concept_key) nests the item, null for a leaf/root; an item's `source` says who added it ('user': the learner, 'agent': a refine, 'emergent': auto-added from notes). `outline` is the learner's raw outline when the track was created with one (a 'draft' for you to tidy), else null. Read-only.

tools.name: jolt_get_pending_corrections
tools.description:
List the learner's correction notes waiting for this sync — the concepts they flagged in the app with "Something's wrong with this concept".
Arguments: none.
Returns: { corrections: [ { concept_id, track_id, title, text, notes: [ { note, created_at } ] } ] }, oldest request first. `text` is the concept as stored; `notes` are the learner's words, oldest first. For each, decide the corrected text (check the source with jolt_get_source_content if needed) and call jolt_correct_concept { track_id, concept_id, text }, which clears the notes. Read-only.

tools.name: jolt_request_upload_url
tools.description:
Mint a short-TTL SAS URL for uploading one source file straight to Blob storage. Jolt compute never receives the bytes — the holder of the URL PUTs them directly. Call this only when you have a file to store; extraction reads existing sources via jolt_get_source_content instead.
Arguments:
  filename (str, required) — original filename; becomes part of the blob path.
  content_type (str, required) — MIME type; one of 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/heic', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf'.
  sha256 (str, required) — hex SHA-256 (64 hex characters) of the exact bytes to be uploaded; confirm hashes the stored bytes and rejects a mismatch.
Returns: { source_id, upload_url }, or { error } for an unsupported content_type or a malformed sha256. The upload_url expires (minutes) and is scoped to exactly one blob path — PUT the bytes to it (at most 25 MiB by default), then the app confirms the upload over REST (POST /v1/uploads/{source_id}/confirm); an unconfirmed source is never offered to a sync. The source stays 'unprocessed' until a sync claims it. Re-calling mints a new source, not a retry of an old one.

tools.name: jolt_log_session
tools.description:
Record a study session and create its concepts, each with a fresh, immediately-due FSRS card so it enters the review rotation at once. This is how extracted material becomes reviewable. Call it once per processed source (or batch of sources) after jolt_store_extraction, before jolt_create_questions.
Arguments:
  source_ids (list[str], required) — the source(s) this session came from; use [] if none. Records provenance for the timeline.
  concepts (list[dict], required) — one dict per concept to create. Each dict:
      text (str, required) — the concept statement to be learned; the atom of recall, one idea per concept. Keep it self-contained.
      track_id (str, required) — the track this concept belongs to (from jolt_get_tracks); must be one of the caller's OWN tracks (curated tracks are read-only). Different concepts in one call may target different tracks.
      title (str, optional) — a short label for the concept.
      syllabus_ref (str, optional) — legacy alias for `concept_key`; used as the concept_key when `concept_key` is omitted. Drives coverage.
      concept_key (str, optional) — the agenda key this concept covers. If it is not yet in the track's agenda syllabus it is AUTO-ADDED (as a leaf, or under `parent`), so the agenda grows to fit what's learned. Auto-add is keyed on concept_key membership, so it is idempotent and skipped on a locked agenda. Falls back to `syllabus_ref` if omitted.
      parent (str, optional) — an existing agenda concept_key to nest this concept under when it is auto-added; ignored if it does not resolve.
      source_id (str, optional) — the specific source this concept came from.
      page (int, optional) — the 1-based page of that source the concept is on (shown to the learner as where it was found).
Raises, writing nothing, if a track is not one of the caller's own or a source id is not one of their sources.
Returns: { session_id, concept_ids }. `concept_ids` are returned in the SAME order as the input `concepts`, so map each returned id back to its concept and pass it as `concept_id` to jolt_create_questions. Creating a concept without questions leaves it due but unanswerable, so always follow with jolt_create_questions. Not idempotent — calling twice creates duplicate concepts; check jolt_get_recent_concepts first if retrying.

tools.name: jolt_set_agenda
tools.description:
Write (replace) a track's agenda syllabus — the refinement step of a sync. ALWAYS read jolt_get_agenda first and build on what's there: this REPLACES the whole syllabus, so anything you omit is dropped. The backend only stores what you send; it never shapes or infers a syllabus — the shaping is yours.
Arguments:
  track_id (str, required) — the track to refine, from jolt_get_tracks.
  syllabus (list[dict], required) — the full replacement syllabus, one dict per item. Each dict:
      concept_key (str, required) — stable key; concepts' syllabus_ref/concept_key join on it. Keep keys stable across refines so coverage and auto-add line up.
      label (str, required) — human-readable topic name.
      parent (str, optional) — another item's concept_key to nest under; omit for a top-level item.
      source (str, optional) — who added this item: 'agent', 'user' or 'emergent'. Omit it: an item whose concept_key already exists keeps its provenance, a new one gets the call's `source`.
  source (str, optional, default 'agent') — who shaped it: 'agent', 'user', or 'emergent'.
  mark_refined (bool, optional, default false) — true to set status='refined' and stamp last_refined_at (use when this is a deliberate refinement pass).
Returns: the updated agenda { status, source, syllabus, last_refined_at, refined_from_source_id, outline }, or { error } if the agenda is LOCKED (locking freezes refinement) or the track is not one of the caller's own (curated tracks are read-only). Replacing with the same syllabus is a safe idempotent no-op. Serialised with the auto-add path under optimistic concurrency, so a concurrent auto-add is never clobbered.

tools.name: jolt_store_extraction
tools.description:
Persist the markdown you extracted from a source and mark the source processed, clearing its sync lease. Call this once per source you claimed via jolt_get_unprocessed_sources, after reading it with jolt_get_source_content and running your own extraction (extraction runs on your compute, not Jolt's).
Arguments:
  source_id (str, required) — the claimed source this extraction is for.
  markdown (str, required) — the full extracted text as markdown.
  confidence (float, optional, default 0.0) — your 0..1 confidence in the extraction's fidelity. Report it honestly: it feeds the silent-misextraction canary metric, so a low value flags a page for human review rather than failing silently.
  model_id (str, optional) — identifier of the model you extracted with, for provenance.
  supersede (bool, optional, default false) — false for a source's FIRST extraction. Set true to replace a source's existing active extraction (a re-extraction) — jolt_get_unprocessed_sources marks those with `supersede: true` (the user asked to read the source again).
  concepts (list[dict], optional) — for a re-extraction, the concepts this read found, so they are RECONCILED against the concepts the previous read produced instead of duplicated. Same fields as jolt_log_session's concepts (text required; title, concept_key, parent, page optional); track_id is optional and defaults to the source's track. Reconciliation is the most dangerous write path — preview it with jolt_diff_extractions first; per concept it is: unchanged (kept), refined (text updated in place, questions and memory kept), changed (a successor concept inherits the memory state; the old one's questions are retired), removed (an old concept with no match leaves the review queue, kept for history), new (a new concept). When you pass `concepts`, do NOT also log them with jolt_log_session.
A source has one active extraction: whichever flag you pass, the new one becomes active and the previous one is kept as a superseded past read. Without `concepts`, log the concepts you found with jolt_log_session, giving each its `source_id`, so they are credited to this read.
Returns: { extraction_id, status ('active'), reconciliation } — reconciliation is null without `concepts`, else { status ('complete'|'partial'), total_steps, applied_steps, remaining_steps, max_steps_per_call, concept_ids, deltas: [ { index, change, concept_id, existing_concept_id, similarity, applied } ] }. `concept_ids` follow your `concepts` order. At most max_steps_per_call (25 by default) concepts are reconciled per call: when status is 'partial', call jolt_continue_reconciliation { source_id } until it is 'complete'. Then write questions (jolt_create_questions) for every delta whose change is 'new' or 'changed'. Returns { error }, storing nothing, when a concept is invalid (no text, or no track_id and the source has none); raises if a track is not the caller's own. Safe to retry: a dropped connection can be re-driven; the source ends processed with the new extraction active (a retry is recorded as one more past read).

tools.name: jolt_create_questions
tools.description:
Attach review questions to a concept. Every concept needs at least one, or it is due but cannot be reviewed. Call after jolt_log_session, using a `concept_id` it returned.
Arguments:
  concept_id (str, required) — the concept these questions test.
  questions (list[dict], required) — one dict per question. Each dict:
      stem (str, required) — the question prompt shown to the learner.
      options (list[str], required) — the multiple-choice options for stage 2. Provide at least two; include the correct option among them.
      correct_index (int, required) — 0-based index into `options` of the correct choice. Must be a valid index into `options`.
      expected_answer (str, required) — the canonical free-text answer. This is the reference the learner's stage-1 free text is graded against (see jolt_get_pending_gradings), so make it a complete, gradeable answer, not just the option label.
Returns: { question_ids } in input order. Raises if the concept is not one of the caller's (they hold no memory state for it). Not idempotent — re-calling adds more questions to the concept.

tools.name: jolt_correct_concept
tools.description:
Replace a single concept's text in place — a small, in-scope wording or accuracy fix that keeps the concept's questions, reviews, and FSRS state intact. Use this for a typo or a clarified sentence, and to answer the learner's correction notes from jolt_get_pending_corrections (re-sending the current text when you judge no change is needed also answers them). NOT for structural change: if the underlying material changed enough that questions or memory state should no longer apply, re-extract with jolt_store_extraction(supersede=true, concepts=...) instead, which reconciles concepts properly.
Arguments:
  track_id (str, required) — the concept's track (concepts are keyed by track, so this is needed to locate it).
  concept_id (str, required) — the concept to edit.
  text (str, required) — the replacement concept text.
Returns: { concept_id, updated, corrections_cleared } — `updated` is false if the write lost a concurrency race (re-read and retry); `corrections_cleared` is how many pending learner notes this answered. Returns { error: 'concept not found' } when the concept does not exist, is not the caller's, or is not on `track_id`.

tools.name: jolt_sync
tools.description:
Start of every unattended sync. Returns the plan — how much work is waiting — so you know whether to proceed and with what batch sizes. Does not claim or change anything.
Arguments:
  limit (int, optional, default 50) — cap on how far to count each queue.
Returns: { unprocessed_sources, pending_gradings, pending_corrections, rereads } — counts (`pending_corrections`: concepts the learner flagged as wrong, read them with jolt_get_pending_corrections), plus `rereads`: [ { source_id, title, preferred_model, requested_at } ], the sources the user asked to read again (already included in unprocessed_sources). Re-extract each with supersede=true. `preferred_model` is the model family the user picked (e.g. 'claude', 'codex') or null for any; it is a preference, not a lock: read it anyway if no other client will.
Typical choreography when counts are non-zero:
  1. jolt_get_unprocessed_sources { limit } — claim a batch.
  2. for each claimed source: jolt_get_source_content -> (extract on your own compute) -> jolt_store_extraction -> jolt_log_session -> jolt_create_questions.
  3. jolt_get_pending_gradings { limit } — claim reviews to grade.
  4. grade each against its expected_answer using the rubric, then jolt_submit_gradings { gradings }.
  5. if pending_corrections > 0: jolt_get_pending_corrections, then jolt_correct_concept for each.
Also tidy any 'draft' agenda that has a learner `outline` (see jolt_get_tracks).
Everything you do runs on the user's own subscription; Jolt only writes rows.

tools.name: jolt_get_unprocessed_sources
tools.description:
Claim a batch of unprocessed sources for extraction, marking each 'in_flight' under a time-limited lease (default ~15 min) so a concurrent sync will not pick up the same rows. You must finish each claimed source by calling jolt_store_extraction, which clears its lease and marks it processed.
Arguments:
  limit (int, optional, default 10) — max sources to claim this call. Match it to how many you can extract before the lease expires.
Returns: { sources: [ { source_id, filename, content_type, lease_expires_at, title, track_id, page_count, supersede, preferred_model } ] }. `page_count` is how many files the upload has (a multi-page note is one source; read every page). `track_id` is the track the user added it to (null if none: pick one). `supersede` true means the source already has an active extraction and the user asked to read it again: store with supersede=true. `preferred_model` is the user's model preference for that re-read, or null. The list may be shorter than `limit` (fewer available, or rows lost to a concurrent claimer). If you crash or the lease expires before you store the extraction, the row becomes claimable again automatically on a later call — no cleanup needed — but after 3 lapsed leases (SOURCE_MAX_ATTEMPTS) the source is marked 'failed' and no longer offered. Next step for each: jolt_get_source_content.

tools.name: jolt_get_pending_gradings
tools.description:
Claim a batch of reviews awaiting a semantic grade — the learner has answered (stage 1 free text + stage 2 choice) and a provisional grade already applied; your job is the authoritative grade of the FREE TEXT against the expected answer, per the versioned rubric.
Arguments:
  limit (int, optional, default 10) — max reviews to claim this call.
Returns: { gradings: [ { review_id, concept_id, question_id, free_text, expected_answer, stem, options, correct_index, question_version, selected_index, is_correct } ], allow_question_rewrite }. `free_text` is the learner's own recall (the graded artefact); `expected_answer` is the reference. Grade the substance of the recall against the reference, not spelling or phrasing. `stem`, `options`, `correct_index` and `question_version` are the question as the learner saw it; `selected_index` / `is_correct` are their multiple-choice pick. `allow_question_rewrite` is the user's opt-in to question rewriting: only when it is true is a `rewritten_question` sent to jolt_submit_gradings stored (otherwise do not write one). Feed each `review_id` and your grade to jolt_submit_gradings. May return fewer than `limit`.

tools.name: jolt_submit_gradings
tools.description:
Submit authoritative FSRS grades for reviews from jolt_get_pending_gradings. Each accepted grade is applied and the affected concept's card is re-folded immediately, which is what lets your semantic grade correct the earlier provisional one.
Arguments:
  gradings (list[dict], required) — one dict per review. Each dict:
      review_id (str, required) — the review being graded, from jolt_get_pending_gradings.
      suggested_fsrs_grade (int, required) — 1=Again, 2=Hard, 3=Good, 4=Easy, chosen per the rubric: grade the free-text recall's substance; when torn between two, pick the LOWER (under-crediting only costs a slightly earlier review, over-crediting silently erodes retention). Any value outside 1..4 is rejected.
      rationale (str, optional) — a short justification for the grade. It is shown to the learner as the feedback on their answer, so address them: one or two plain sentences on what their recall got right or missed.
      rubric_version (str, optional) — the rubric version string you graded against, stamped for audit.
      rewritten_question (dict, optional) — only when jolt_get_pending_gradings said allow_question_rewrite=true: a better next version of the question, tuned to how the learner answered (e.g. probe the part they missed, or ask from a new angle once they clearly know it). Same fields as in jolt_create_questions: stem (str), options (list[str], at least two), correct_index (int, valid index into options), expected_answer (str), plus rewrite_reason (str, optional) — one short sentence the learner sees on why the question changed. It becomes version n+1 of the question (old versions are kept, not edited) and the old version leaves the review queue. Omit it when the question is fine as it is.
Returns: { applied, submitted, rewritten, rewrites_skipped } — `submitted` is how many you sent, `applied` how many were newly graded; `rewritten` lists each version created: [ { review_id, question_id (the new version), version, previous_version_id } ]; `rewrites_skipped` lists each rewrite not stored, with a reason (rewriting is off for this user, invalid fields, review already graded). A skipped rewrite never blocks the grade. Idempotent per review_id: re-submitting an already-graded review is a safe no-op (counted in `submitted`, not `applied`; a rewrite it created is listed again, never duplicated), so retrying after a dropped connection never double-writes.

tools.name: jolt_list_sources
tools.description:
List all of the caller's sources with their processing status — an overview for deciding what to (re-)extract.
Arguments: none.
Returns: { sources: [ { source_id, filename, processing_status, active_extraction_id, page_count, reread_requested } ] } where processing_status is 'unprocessed', 'in_flight' (claimed by a sync), 'processed', or 'failed' (could not be read after repeated attempts). `active_extraction_id` is the current canonical extraction, or null if never extracted. `reread_requested` is true while the user's read-again request is pending. Uploads that were never confirmed are left out. Read-only — does not claim anything (use jolt_get_unprocessed_sources to claim for extraction).

tools.name: jolt_get_source_content
tools.description:
Get a short-TTL signed GET URL to read a source's original bytes, so you can run extraction on your own compute. Call it for each source you claimed via jolt_get_unprocessed_sources (or any source you want to re-read for a supersede).
Arguments:
  source_id (str, required) — the source to read.
Returns: { source_id, filename, content_type, read_url, page_count, pages: [ { index, filename, content_type, read_url } ] }. A multi-page note is one source with several files: read every entry of `pages`, in `index` order, and extract them together as one note. The top-level filename / content_type / read_url are the first page's. Read URLs expire in minutes — fetch promptly and re-call for fresh ones if they lapse. Use each page's `content_type` to decide how to parse (PDF vs image). Read-only; does not change the source's processing status.

tools.name: jolt_diff_extractions
tools.description:
Preview the per-concept reconciliation a re-extraction WOULD produce, without writing anything. Run this before jolt_store_extraction(supersede=true) to see how your proposed concepts line up against the track's existing ones, so a supersede never silently discards memory state.
Arguments:
  track_id (str, required) — the track whose active concepts to diff against (the caller's own concepts on it; raises if the track is neither the caller's nor curated).
  proposed_concepts (list[dict], required) — the concepts your new extraction would create. Each dict: text (str, required), title (str, optional), syllabus_ref (str, optional) — same fields as jolt_log_session concepts.
Returns: { deltas: [ { change, existing_concept_id, proposed_text, similarity } ] } where `change` is one of:
    unchanged — matches an existing concept; no-op on commit.
    refined  — minor edit; existing concept's text updates, keeping its questions, reviews, and FSRS state.
    changed  — materially different; existing concept is superseded by a successor that carries the state forward, its old questions retired.
    removed  — an existing concept with no match in your proposal; superseded and dropped from the due queue but kept for history.
    new      — no existing match; a new concept (generate questions for it).
`similarity` is the 0..1 text-match score behind the classification. Read-only. If the diff is not what you intend, adjust `proposed_concepts` before committing the supersede.

tools.name: jolt_continue_reconciliation
tools.description:
Resume a re-extraction's concept reconciliation that jolt_store_extraction(concepts=...) left 'partial' — a large supersede is applied at most max_steps_per_call concepts per call from a saved checkpoint, so an interrupted one is never half-lost.
Arguments:
  source_id (str, required) — the re-extracted source.
Returns: the same reconciliation object as jolt_store_extraction { status, total_steps, applied_steps, remaining_steps, max_steps_per_call, concept_ids, deltas }. Call again while status is 'partial'. Safe to repeat: a complete reconciliation is returned unchanged, and a step interrupted mid-way converges when resumed. Returns { error } when the source's active read has no reconciliation (it was stored without `concepts`); raises if the source is not the caller's.
